subject: TTFT & sustained throughput: SLA alignment for streaming vs sync endpoints
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@finservbank.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finservbank.com
Date: 2027-02-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify TTFT vs sustained tokens expectations for our POC

Camila,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — the team liked the streaming demo, but procurement needs us to be explicit in the SLA about two things before we move to legal: (1) our measurable Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints and how that is measured, and (2) sustained token/sec expectations for high-throughput inference (we have a compliance window where the model must process 1k+ tokens/sec for sustained periods).

A few clarifying questions from their side:
- Do you measure TTFT to the client-facing socket first byte, or to the first completed token chunk at the application level?
- How do you define sustained throughput in a mixed workload (many short chat calls + some long batch streams)? Is there a p50/p95 expectation we can quote?
- Are there documented fallback behaviors (e.g., switch to a higher-latency but higher-throughput sync endpoint) and how those are handled in the SLA?

I'm attaching our internal SLA redlines. Can you respond with concrete numbers we can circulate? Procurement wants concrete metrics rather than vague language.

Best,
Alice
Alice Jenkins
Director, Platform Ops
FinservBank

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@finservbank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Clarify TTFT vs sustained tokens expectations for our POC

Thanks Alice — appreciate the clear list. High level answers up front and then specifics below so procurement has something to put in the draft.

High level:
- TTFT (streaming): measured at the client socket as the time from request accept to first token bytes transmitted on the stream. Standard measurement surface: p50/p95 over a rolling 1h window per route/model.
- TTFT (sync): measured as time from request accept to first byte of the full payload (we treat non-streaming as single-response; p95 targets are typically higher than streaming because of aggregation).
- Sustained throughput: we define sustained token/sec over configurable windows (default 60s and 5m) with p50/p95 reporting. We can set contract-level sustained thresholds and burst allowances.

Concrete proposed numbers (initial suggestion we can negotiate):
- Streaming endpoint TTFT: p50 <= 220 ms, p95 <= 420 ms for sequences <= 512 tokens on our Dedicated tier in us-west region.
- Sync endpoint TTFT (first byte of full payload): p50 <= 650 ms, p95 <= 1.5 s for standard generation requests (<=1024 tokens).
- Sustained throughput (per instance pool): baseline sustained 800 tokens/sec (60s window) with p95 >= 700 tokens/sec. Burst allowance up to 1,200 tokens/sec sustained for up to 90s, subject to available burst capacity.

Fallbacks / degradation policies:
- If streaming pool is saturated, traffic is automatically routed to a compatible model variant in Dedicated or to a sync endpoint depending on route policy and customer tolerance for latency. Such automatic fallback will be logged and surfaced in Console; we can include a 30-day lookback in reports.
- We can include a clause that routing/fallbacks will not be considered SLA violations if customer chooses a lower-tier model or custom routing policy that reduces available capacity.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa for technical confirmation + to propose wording suitable for legal. If these numbers won't work, tell me which specific thresholds Finserv needs and we will draft a carveout proposal.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Clarify TTFT vs sustained tokens expectations for our POC

Adding tech detail for procurement/legal:

Measurement surface and definitions (so the SLA wording is unambiguous):
- TTFT (streaming): measured from server-side request accept timestamp (when request is validated and enqueued for runtime) to first token bytes transmitted to the downstream socket. This includes internal queuing and model scheduling time. We report p50/p95/p99 on a per-route and per-model basis, with a 1-hour sliding window for enforcement charts and a 24-hour aggregate for monthly SLA calculations.
- TTFT (sync/non-streaming): measured from server-side request accept to the first byte of the response payload sent to the client. For sync requests where payload is generated in a single pass, TTFT is effectively the end-to-end generation latency.
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec): defined as tokens emitted by the model divided by wall time across a customer-dedicated pool, computed in both 60s and 300s windows. We will publish p50/p95 across those windows.

Performance guarantees and exceptions:
- For Dedicated deployments: we commit to the numbers Camila proposed (streaming p50 <= 220 ms, p95 <= 420 ms for <=512 tokens). For multi-tenant Hosted customers we provide best-effort targets and recommend Dedicated for contractual SLA.
- Noise floor: short bursty mixtures (many concurrent short chats) can reduce observed sustained token/sec for any single session; we guarantee pool-level sustained rates rather than per-session sustained rates unless otherwise specified.
- Throttles and backpressure: if a customer's session exceeds configured per-session token-rate caps, the runtime applies graceful backpressure (reduced token emission rate) and includes a header on the stream indicating throttling. We can include this behavior as an allowed mitigation in the SLA so it isn't treated as a full outage.

Suggested legal wording snippets (for insertion in SLA):
"Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints is measured at the network socket and reported as p50/p95 over a 1-hour sliding window. TTFT commitments apply to requests not exceeding 512 generation tokens. Exceptions: model cold starts, customer-requested low-priority routing, or force-failover events are excluded from TTFT calculations if documented in the incident report."

"Sustained token throughput is measured at the pool level in 60s and 300s windows. We commit to a baseline sustained throughput of 800 tokens/sec (60s window) on Dedicated pools, with burst allowance to 1,200 tokens/sec for up to 90s. Sustained throughput applies to standard generation workloads and excludes synthetic load tests or inventorying scans performed without prior notice."

Open items we should confirm with Finserv:
- Are their "sustained" expectations per logical user session (per customer conversation) or per account/pool? (We recommend pool-level.)
- Do they require guarantees across regional failover (cross-region)? If so, the numbers change due to added routing latency and potential cold-start costs.

I'll defer to Marissa on whether the proposed p95 numbers are acceptable for our Dedicated capacity commitments and whether we should carve out additional language for long-tail (>=2k token) generations.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Camila / Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail procurement and our SRE team needed, thank you. A couple quick notes from ops:
- We can accept pool-level sustained guarantees (preferred).
- For the POC we're going to ask for a temporary carveout: sustained 1,000 tokens/sec (60s) with burst to 1,500 tokens/sec for 120s so we can validate under expected peak traffic. If results are within tolerance, we'll move to the baseline 800 tokens/sec commitment in production and sign the Dedicated contract.
- Can you add language that any automatic routing/fallbacks will be flagged in the Console with a clear "fallback_reason" tag and incident id? That will help our audit team during the POC.

If you can provide an updated redline with the temporary POC carveout and the Console tag requirement, we can circulate to legal.

Regards,
